title: 本地人不愿意参观博物馆：个人原稿与反馈
original:
It is said that people are losing their enthusiasm for visiting local museums and places of historical importance. This essay will put forward explanations for this before suggesting solutions to tackling this problem.

There are many reasons why museums and historical places are not frequented by local people. The main one is that local people find paying a visit to local tourist attractions boring and a waste of time. In other words, such places would be visually unattractive and arouse little interest in locals, for the simple reason that they have been familiar with those places through school courses or personal experiences. Another significant reason is that the authorities charge a substantial amount of admission fee, giving rise to a reduction of the number of locals visiting historic sites. As a result, the destinations would be generally more appealing and worthy to the tourists than to the locals.

To encourage local residents to attend historical relics and museums, several measures can be prompted. First and foremost, authorities can change the perception of museums and historical sites by organizing cultural events and regular exhibitions, including weddings, concerts and celebrations. These renewals would provide the public with a new experience and attract media attention to historical values. Another solution is to offer free tickets and special promotions for local people at weekends. For example, the Confucian temple in China has set specific days on which free entrance is available for everyone to commemorate and honour traditional occasions. In conclusion, people avoid visiting museums or historical places due to their familiarity with those destinations and high entrance fees. The government can promote these sites by conducting interesting programmes and offering free or subsidised entry.
feedback: 主要修正：题干只说明游客多于当地居民，不宜擅自写成热情正在下降；familiar 不等于 visually unattractive；attend museums 应改为 visit museums；measures can be prompted 搭配错误；补足“游客愿意为一次性体验付费，而居民不愿反复为熟悉景点付费”的比较逻辑。第三段末尾原稿存在句子残缺。
model:
Museums and historical sites often attract more tourists than local residents. This may be because local people are less interested in familiar attractions and because admission fees can discourage regular visits. Several measures could help address this problem.

One major reason is that local residents may find museums and historical sites less interesting than tourists do. Having learned about these places at school or visited them before, they may feel that there is little new to discover. Tourists, however, are often eager to explore unfamiliar history and culture. Another reason is that local authorities sometimes charge high admission fees. While tourists may consider these costs worthwhile during a short trip, local residents may be less willing to pay repeatedly to visit familiar attractions.

Several measures could encourage more local residents to visit. Firstly, museums and historical sites could organise regularly changing exhibitions, cultural events and workshops. These activities would provide fresh experiences and encourage people to rediscover their local heritage. Secondly, local authorities could offer free admission days or discounted tickets for residents. For example, historic temples could provide free entry during traditional festivals, allowing local people to take part in cultural activities without paying an admission fee. Such measures could increase local interest and make these attractions more accessible.

In conclusion, familiarity and high admission fees may discourage local people from visiting museums and historical sites. More engaging activities and affordable entry could help attract residents and strengthen their connection to local heritage.

title: 纸质报纸和书籍是否会消失：个人作文（节选存档）
original:
It is true that more and more people choose to read online rather than physical books nowadays, however I don’t consider printed books or newspapers would necessarily disappear in the future. Because physical books won’t be replaced both for individuals and society, especially in some special circumstance.

A growing number of people preferring electronic books can mainly attributed to its convenience and cost-effectiveness. People can obtain instant massages and keep up with the world just trough their phone. It has developed to a daily habit that people are used to check their phone at the first second after waking up. The news happened in other side of the world can transport over the world within one hour. In addition, people can scroll some articles and novels just during their commutes or their waiting time, without carrying heavy books with them. On top of that, price of electronic books can be quite affordable than physical books and many online articles are even open freely to public, which saving a large part of cost for people. As a result, there are more and more people change to online reading.

However, even though the advantages of digital reading are obvious, the function of physical books and newspapers can’t be replaced totally. Firstly, the messages are more reliable in this way because there are specialized staff checking the information source and the printing mistakes before open to public. And these reliable messages can be quite important especially in some public urgent circumstance. For example, many online message came out instantly during the period of covid-19, while many unjustified messages misleading people and resulting in public panic. However the information from newspapers can give people comfort and inform them the important regulations. Moreover, the users of physical newspaper and books are mainly old generations because they are not comfortable of using digital device. Therefore, we should also take the requirements of these people into consideration.

Overall, although reading online have the benefits to people, we should combine it with physical books and newspapers rather than replacement of that. Physical books and newspapers have their necessity to exist and can bring more advantages than drawbacks to individuals and society.
feedback: 高频错误：be attributed to；be used to doing；access the latest news；freely available to the public；printed publications；reputable newspapers；be comfortable using；结论须回答 nobody will buy，不能错答成优缺点。
model: 范文修订见本项目原对话。本网页保留个人原稿和本轮纠错重点；不把新的概括误称为用户原文。

title: 拥有房产 vs 租房：个人作文（节选存档）
original:
Many people choose to buy a house or flat rather than renting one in some countries, which can be attributed to personal pursuring and social background. This essay will examine the potential caues of it and argue that, on balance, it brings more drawbacks to individuals and society if regarding owning a home as a neccessary requirement.

It's understandable that owning a home can provide a sense of stability and satisfaction in some countries. Owning a house or flat means you have a place to stay when you face with difficulties like unemployment and going broke. You don't need to figure out the renting expenditure and it will definitely give you a stable backing up force. In addition, owning a home even is a symbol of satisfaction for most ordinary peope, and someone takes it as an important goal through a long period, for example, owning a home becomes a former condition of marriage for many Chinese. As a result, owning a home can be associated with a stable life and an ideal statuse due to their value and social background.

However, it also gives too much pressure especailly for younge people lack enough finance. Younge people not only need to face with the intensive job market competition, they also need to undertake the pressure of buying a home. And the price of a home can be quite expensive so they can't pay once or by themselves. As a result, many of them have to lend money from their families or even from loan companies, resulting in much more living pressure. Moreover, some younge couples may afraid of getting marriage and giving birth because of the heavy pressue of buying a home, leading to a low marriage rate and birth rate. That's why many younge people choose to live in a rent home rather than spending all their savings buying one. Personally, I think a home is just a place to live, it shouldn't become a must in life.

In conclusion, owning a house can provide a lot benefits to people, while wheather buying one or renting one should depend on the personal situation. Both of these two ways can lead to a well-being life if someone can arrange their money reasonably and take responsibility to their own life.
feedback: 高频错误：face difficulties vs be faced with difficulties；borrow from vs lend to；take out a mortgage；be a prerequisite for marriage；place considerable pressure on；结论应强调 treating home ownership as a necessity 的社会压力。

title: 澳大利亚年龄与就业率：个人原稿、完整批改与双版本
type: Task 1 · 折线图 · 练习估分约5.5
original:
The line graph compares the percentages of employees aged 18 to 34 in terms of men and women in Australia, in 1976 and 2011.

Overall, the employment rate increased as age growing older, expecting the proportion of women employmees in 2011, with a fluctuate trend among ages. While the emolyment rates of men were leading that for women in both years, through age 18 to 34.

In 1976, the men employment proportion rose from 70% in age 18 to 92% approximatedly in age 34, while that for women workers growed from 63% in age 18 to 71% in age 43, with a smoother increasing trend in general.

However, the emoloyment rates for these two sexual were overly fell in 2011, compared with that in 1976. The number of men employees increased steadily along with the age growing, the proportion rising from 60% in age 18 to 75% in age 34. However, the figure for women in 2011 rose to 58% in age 23 before felling to only 54% in age 28. Then, the women employees proportion increased back to 55% in the age of 34, representing the highest figure for women employees in 2011.
feedback:
这篇原稿的练习估分约为 **Band 5.5**。你按 **1976 年、2011 年**分段的思路合理，也看出了 **2011 年女性就业率先升、后降、再回升**。最影响提分的是把这条线的**最终回升读成了 55%**，以及在概述里漏掉了一个全图规律：**在每个年龄点，男女各自的就业率在 2011 年都低于 1976 年。**

## 一、整体评分与任务分析

这是一张**按年龄比较就业率的折线图**。横轴是 **18–34 岁**，图例是 **1976 年和 2011 年**。写同一条线时，用 *at age 18 … at age 34* 比较不同年龄。比较年份时，用 *in 2011 … in 1976*，并保持性别和年龄一致。

| 官方评分维度 | 练习估分 | 原文依据与提分方向 |
|---|---:|---|
| **Task Achievement** | 5–6 | 概述识别了男性高于女性和 2011 年女性曲线的例外。但 2011 年男性终值、女性回升后的终值和若干转折点读错，影响了关键特征的呈现。 |
| **Coherence and Cohesion** | 6 | 四段分工明确。按年份分段可行，但最后一段连续使用 *However*，第一个表示跨年对比，第二个实际是在转向女性组。 |
| **Lexical Resource** | 5 | 有 *rose from … to …*、*the figure for women* 等准确表达。*employees proportion*、*these two sexual* 和多处拼写错误降低了精确度。 |
| **Grammatical Range and Accuracy** | 5 | 尝试了 *while*、比较替代和 *before + -ing*，但出现了独立的 *While* 从句、*were fell*、*growed*、*felling* 等错误。 |

**最影响提分的三件事**是①先校对曲线末端和转折点；②在概述里同时说明**年龄规律、性别差距和年份差异**；③固定用 **employment rate + 谓语** 描述比例，并区分 *at age 18* 和 *in 1976*。

## 二、逐段批改

### P1 · Introduction

> The line graph compares the percentages of employees aged 18 to 34 in terms of men and women in Australia, in 1976 and 2011.

| 我的原表达 | 错误原因 | 推荐修改 | 知识点总结 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `the percentages of employees aged 18 to 34` | 容易理解成“雇员当中 18–34 岁的人所占的比例”。图中的分母是**相应年龄和性别的人群**。 | **the employment rates of Australian men and women aged 18 to 34** | **employment rate** 直接点明指标。也可写 *the percentage of people in employment*。 |
| `in terms of men and women in Australia, in 1976 and 2011` | 性别可以直接接在 *employment rates of* 后面，最后一个逗号也可以去掉。 | **the employment rates of men and women aged 18 to 34 in Australia in 1976 and 2011** | 图中只给两个年份，用 **in 1976 and 2011** 准确交代范围。 |

### P2 · Overview

> Overall, the employment rate increased as age growing older, expecting the proportion of women employmees in 2011, with a fluctuate trend among ages. While the emolyment rates of men were leading that for women in both years, through age 18 to 34.

| 我的原表达 | 错误原因 | 推荐修改 | 知识点总结 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `increased as age growing older` | `as` 在这里引出从句，原句缺限定动词。图表比较不同年龄的人群，可以直接用 *with age*。 | **Employment rates generally rose with age.** | **rise with age** 简明地表达年龄越高，数值总体越高。 |
| `expecting … with a fluctuate trend` | “除了”用 **except**。**fluctuate** 是动词，*a fluctuate trend* 词形错误。 | **… except among women in 2011, whose employment rate fluctuated.** | **except among + 人群**。写细节时，用 *rose, dipped and then recovered* 说明波动形态。 |
| `While the … rates of men were leading that for women …` | *While* 从句缺主句。*were leading* 在这里不如 *were higher than* 自然。若前文用复数 *rates*，替代时用 **those**。 | **Men’s employment rates were higher than those of women at every age in both years.** | **those of women** 代替 *the employment rates of women*。强调同年龄比较，用 **at every age**。 |

### P3 · Detail 1

> In 1976, the men employment proportion rose from 70% in age 18 to 92% approximatedly in age 34, while that for women workers growed from 63% in age 18 to 71% in age 43, with a smoother increasing trend in general.

| 我的原表达 | 错误原因 | 推荐修改 | 知识点总结 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `the men employment proportion` | 名词组合不自然，且 *men* 和 *employment* 的关系没有表达清楚。 | **the employment rate for men** / **the male employment rate** | 第一次点明指标，后面可接 **the figure for women**。 |
| `70% in age 18 to 92% approximatedly in age 34` | 年龄用 **at age**。拼写是 **approximately**，通常放在数字前。 | **from 70% at age 18 to around 92% at age 34** | **from X to Y** 表示起终值。也可写 *among 18-year-olds*。 |
| `that for women workers growed … in age 43` | **`that for` 的结构用对了**，它可以承接前面的单数 *rate*。动词过去式是 *grew*，终点年龄应为 **34**。 | **while that for women rose from about 63% at age 18 to around 71% at age 34** | **the rate for men → that for women**。用 **women** 就能标明比较组。 |
| `with a smoother increasing trend in general` | *smoother* 暗示变化更均匀，但女性曲线上有数段持平。你观察到的更明显的区别是**增幅较小**。 | **The increase among women was much smaller.** | 男性约增加 **22 个百分点**，女性约增加 **8 个百分点**。比较幅度可以用 **a smaller increase**。 |

### P4 · Detail 2

> However, the emoloyment rates for these two sexual were overly fell in 2011, compared with that in 1976. The number of men employees increased steadily along with the age growing, the proportion rising from 60% in age 18 to 75% in age 34. However, the figure for women in 2011 rose to 58% in age 23 before felling to only 54% in age 28. Then, the women employees proportion increased back to 55% in the age of 34, representing the highest figure for women employees in 2011.

| 我的原表达 | 错误原因 | 推荐修改 | 知识点总结 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `the … rates for these two sexual were overly fell … compared with that` | **sexual** 是形容词。*were fell* 混用了 **were lower** 和 **fell**。复数 *rates* 用 **those** 承接。 | **In 2011, employment rates for both men and women were lower than those recorded in 1976 at every age.** | 对比两个年份的水平，**were lower than** 最直接。图表只给两个年份，无法判断期间是否持续下降。 |
| `The number of men employees increased … to 75% in age 34` | 图中是**就业率**。2011 年男性在 **30 岁约为 75%**，到 **34 岁是 80%**。 | **The male employment rate rose steadily with age, from 60% at age 18 to 80% at age 34.** | 报终值前，沿着正确颜色的曲线找到最右端，再核对横轴年龄。 |
| `rose to 58% in age 23 before felling to only 54% in age 28` | 读图约为 **23–24 岁 57%**、**28–29 岁 53%**。*fall* 的 -ing 形式是 **falling**。 | **It reached around 57% at ages 23 and 24 before falling to about 53% at ages 28 and 29.** | **before falling to + 终值**。连续两个年龄读数相同时，可以合写。 |
| `increased back to 55% … representing the highest figure` | 34 岁的点约为 **59%**。你判断“达到该组最高值”的方向是对的，问题在于 **55%** 这个读数。 | **It then climbed to about 59% at age 34, the highest figure for women in 2011.** | **climbed to** 适合这里的回升。**returned to** 适合回到先前达到过的同一水平。 |

## 三、数据取舍与 Overview

图上没有逐点标注百分比。下表中 **63%、57%、53%、59%** 等读数来自刻度估读，正文用 *about* 或 *around*。

| 要说明的特征 | 优先选的数据 | 为什么这样选 |
|---|---|---|
| **男性两条线随年龄上升，1976 年始终较高** | 1976 年 **70% → 约 92%**，2011 年 **60% → 80%** | 两组起终点都用 **18 岁和 34 岁**，可以同时看出年龄方向和年份差异。中间年龄无需逐一列出。 |
| **1976 年女性就业率增幅较小** | **约 63% → 约 71%** | 和同年的男性起终值配对后，读者可以看出男性与女性的差距由约 **7 个百分点**扩大到约 **21 个百分点**。正文可写起终值，或再补一句差距，无需把两种比较各写一遍。 |
| **2011 年女性曲线先升、后降、再回升** | 18 岁约 **53%**，23–24 岁约 **57%**，28–29 岁约 **53%**，34 岁约 **59%** | **57% → 53% → 59%** 是这条线最有辨识度的形状。若篇幅有限，省去 18 岁的起点仍能写清三个阶段。 |
| **年份和性别的比较范围** | 同年、同龄下男性高于女性。同龄、同性别下 1976 年高于 2011 年。 | 这两条适合放进概述。图中约 19–20 岁的交叉发生在 **2011 年男性**与 **1976 年女性**之间，不影响同年男女比较，正文可省略。 |

你的 **Overview** 已经找到了“总体随年龄上升”和“2011 年女性例外”。优化时，加上**两个年份的水平差异**，并明确性别比较是在**同一年、同一年龄**下进行的。

> **Overall, employment rates generally rose with age, although the figure for women in 2011 fluctuated. At every age, men had higher employment rates than women in both years, and the rates for both sexes were lower in 2011 than in 1976.**

## 四、可复制的错题库与高频表达

| 分类 | 错误表达 → 正确表达 → 使用场景 → 示例句 |
|---|---|
| 趋势词汇 | `a fluctuate trend` → **fluctuated** → 有升有降 → *The female employment rate fluctuated in 2011.* |
| 数据比较 | `the number of men employees rose to 80%` → **the male employment rate rose to 80%** → 纵轴是百分比 → *The male employment rate reached 80% at age 34.* |
| 固定搭配 | `as age growing older` → **with age** → 横轴是年龄 → *The rate rose steadily with age.* |
| 时态与词形 | `were overly fell` → **were generally lower** → 比较两组已经结束的年份 → *Employment rates were lower in 2011 than in 1976.* |
| 冠词、单复数和介词 | `in age 18` → **at age 18** → 交代某个年龄点 → *The figure stood at 70% at age 18.* |
| 从句与衔接 | `While the rates of men were higher.` → **Men’s rates were higher, while women’s rates varied more by age in 2011.** → 用 *while* 连接两个完整分句。 |

**本题最值得积累的 10 个表达**

| 表达 | 可迁移例句 |
|---|---|
| **the employment rate for [group]** | *The employment rate for men reached 80% at age 34.* |
| **at every age shown** | *Men’s employment rates were higher at every age shown in both years.* |
| **rise steadily with age** | *The male employment rate rose steadily with age in 2011.* |
| **rise from X to Y** | *The figure rose from 60% to 80%.* |
| **increase more modestly** | *The rate for women increased more modestly in 1976.* |
| **that for [group]** | *The male employment rate was higher than that for women in 1976.* |
| **those recorded in [year]** | *The rates in 2011 were lower than those recorded in 1976.* |
| **stand at around X** | *The figure for women stood at around 53% at age 18 in 2011.* |
| **reach X before falling to Y** | *The figure reached around 57% before falling to about 53%.* |
| **reach its highest point at age X** | *The female employment rate in 2011 reached its highest point at age 34.* |

## 五、两个修改版本

### 版本 A · 保留原意的修正版

保留你按 **1976 年 → 2011 年**组织正文的方式。

> The line graph compares the employment rates of men and women aged 18 to 34 in Australia in 1976 and 2011.
>
> Overall, employment rates generally rose with age, although the rate for women in 2011 fluctuated. Men recorded higher rates than women at every age in both years. For both sexes, employment rates were lower in 2011 than in 1976 at every age shown.
>
> In 1976, the employment rate for men rose from 70% at age 18 to approximately 92% at age 34. The figure for women also rose, but by a much smaller amount, from around 63% to 71% over the same age range.
>
> In 2011, the male employment rate rose steadily with age, from 60% at age 18 to 80% at age 34. The figure for women, meanwhile, increased from around 53% at age 18 to about 57% at ages 23 and 24 before falling to around 53% at ages 28 and 29. It then climbed to approximately 59% at age 34, the highest figure for women that year.

### 版本 B · Band 7.5–8 目标版

这一版按**男性、女性**分段，约 **180 词**。每段都在同一性别内比较两个年份，让四条线的关系更容易看清。

> The line graph compares employment rates among Australian men and women aged 18 to 34 in 1976 and 2011.
>
> Overall, employment rates generally rose with age, although the figure for women in 2011 fluctuated. Men were more likely to be employed than women of the same age in both years. For each sex, rates were lower in 2011 than in 1976 across the entire age range.
>
> Among men, employment rates rose steadily with age in both years. In 1976, the figure climbed from 70% at age 18 to approximately 92% at age 34. The corresponding figures for 2011 were 60% and 80%, respectively.
>
> The rise with age among women was more modest in 1976, with the rate increasing from about 63% at age 18 to around 71% at age 34. In 2011, the female rate started at about 53% and reached around 57% at ages 23 and 24. It then dipped back to about 53% at ages 28 and 29 before climbing to 59% at age 34, its highest point that year.

## 六、复盘与短句训练

**本次最值得记住的五点**：①年龄用 **at age**，年份用 **in**。②指标是比例时用 **employment rate**。③切换组别可用 **that for women**，承接多项就业率用 **those**。④描述曲线起伏可用 **rose … before falling …**。⑤概述写总体关系，正文挑起终值和关键转折点作证。

**你这篇最易重复的三个问题**是年龄点与数值错配、名词和动词形式混用，以及用 *while* 开头后缺主句。

> **个人易错点记录｜Task 1 · 年龄与就业率**  
> `in age 34` → `at age 34`  
> `a fluctuate trend` → `the rate fluctuated`  
> `were fell` → `were lower`  
> `before felling to` → `before falling to`  
> **读图复核**：先对图例，再确认该点的横轴年龄和纵轴百分比。2011 年两条线在 34 岁分别为男性 **80%**、女性约 **59%**。

**短句练习**

1. 改错：*The number of male employees rose from 60% in age 18 to 80% in age 34.*
2. 用 **those** 改错：*The employment rates in 2011 were lower than that in 1976.*
3. 把两句用 **while** 合并：*The male employment rate rose steadily with age in 2011. The female rate fluctuated.*
4. 用 **before falling to** 翻译：2011 年，女性就业率在 23–24 岁达到约 57%，随后在 28–29 岁降至约 53%。

**参考答案**

1. The male employment rate rose from 60% **at age 18** to 80% **at age 34**.
2. Employment rates in 2011 were lower than **those recorded in 1976**.
3. The male employment rate rose steadily with age in 2011, **while the female rate fluctuated**.
4. In 2011, the female employment rate reached around 57% at ages 23 and 24 **before falling to** about 53% at ages 28 and 29.
model:
版本 A · 保留原意修正版

The line graph compares the employment rates of men and women aged 18 to 34 in Australia in 1976 and 2011.

Overall, employment rates generally rose with age, although the rate for women in 2011 fluctuated. Men recorded higher rates than women at every age in both years. For both sexes, employment rates were lower in 2011 than in 1976 at every age shown.

In 1976, the employment rate for men rose from 70% at age 18 to approximately 92% at age 34. The figure for women also rose, but by a much smaller amount, from around 63% to 71% over the same age range.

In 2011, the male employment rate rose steadily with age, from 60% at age 18 to 80% at age 34. The line graph compares employment rates among Australian men and women aged 18 to 34 in 1976 and 2011.

Overall, employment rates generally rose with age, although the figure for women in 2011 fluctuated. Men were more likely to be employed than women of the same age in both years. For each sex, rates were lower in 2011 than in 1976 across the entire age range.

Among men, employment rates rose steadily with age in both years. In 1976, the figure climbed from 70% at age 18 to approximately 92% at age 34. The corresponding figures for 2011 were 60% and 80%, respectively.

The rise with age among women was more modest in 1976, with the rate increasing from about 63% at age 18 to around 71% at age 34. In 2011, the female rate started at about 53% and reached around 57% at ages 23 and 24. It then dipped back to about 53% at ages 28 and 29 before climbing to 59% at age 34, its highest point that year.
